BERT4Rec deployment checks must preserve masked-item semantics. [RecTools’ implementation](https://rectools.readthedocs.io/en/stable/_modules/rectools/models/nn/transformers/bert4rec.html) explicitly uses left padding, truncates history to reserve one position, and appends MASK for inference. For this task, verify identical prepared tensors in training-side evaluation and working/predict.py: padding/mask IDs, truncation, positions and attention masks. Read the final nonpadding position—the appended MASK—never nonzero-count minus one. Include short, maximum-length and repeated-item histories; ensure PAD/MASK cannot appear as recommended items.

An inexpensive differential test: compare the selected in-memory model with the deployed predictor loading that exact checkpoint, using identical histories and ordered candidates in each category. Check architecture configuration, strict state-dict loading, item-map round trips, category-to-checkpoint routing, intermediate features and candidate scores. PyTorch documents [state-dict restoration and eval mode](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/saving_loading_models); use [assert_close](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/testing.html) with explicit tolerances and separately inspect ranking differences near ties. These are proposed checks, not measured results.

[2025 model-level metamorphic-testing research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.04354) supports testing equivalent executions. Applicable proposed relations: candidate permutation permutes scores identically; duplicated candidates receive equal scores; batch permutation permutes outputs; isolated versus batched requests agree within tolerance; save/reload preserves outputs. Arbitrary padding shifts are not necessarily invariant with absolute positional embeddings. Cross-device bitwise equality is [not guaranteed](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html). Checkpoint parity, actual mappings, routing and predictor internals remain unavailable without executing or inspecting the supplied artifacts; report unavailable checks explicitly, never as passes.
